assessments.reasoning: The four-part SPDX detail has SHA-256 70a192d0ffeed7a110075f58cc536ff3a976ca8e7fbdb545ac6496ee62de15c7. Part 1 supplies the SA 1.0 text, draft wording and false deprecation flag. Part 2 gives licenseId CC-SA-1.0, the name, both exact URL citations and match="true".
The unsigned annotated v3.29.0 tag in spdx/license-list-data targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, which pins the inspected json/details/CC-SA-1.0.json.

The cited unsuffixed URL matches the publisher acquisition exactly. The captured heading “ShareAlike 1.0 Generic” and identifier “CC SA 1.0” identify its subject. The retirement notice and the separate legalcode.en canonical are visible in that capture.

The publisher’s introductory fine print says “DISTRIBUTION OF THIS DRAFT LICENSE DOES NOT CREATE AN ATTORNEY-CLIENT RELATIONSHIP.” SPDX repeats the wording in licenseText. The repetition shares the publisher lineage and supports retaining the qualification without resolving its legal significance.

challenge.method: Compared the SPDX ID, name, licenseText and template with the publisher heading. Checked whether retirement, draft wording, or the absence of “Generic” from the plain-text heading defeats the citation.
challenge.results: The SPDX name is “Creative Commons Share Alike 1.0 Generic”. Its licenseText heading says “ShareAlike 1.0” and its template makes “Generic” optional. The publisher heading includes “Generic”. The exact ID and literal citation survive these differences. Neither the recorded match="true" nor the deprecation flag resolves finality.

limitations: The draft notice’s significance, finality and legal effect remain unresolved. The exact citation establishes no byte or legal equivalence with legalcode.en, publisher currency, project applicability, downstream rights, permission to redistribute text or installation eligibility.
